content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Model underestimates prices in the latter part of the forecast, particularly when true values show strong upward momentum.
- Forecasts tend to lag behind true price movements, especially in the 10–20 day range.
- Overshoots occur after sharp price increases; model reacts too quickly and peaks too high.
- Mean reversion is not adequately captured — model fails to adjust downward when prices are over 70–75 after a spike.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values in the 30-day forecast, especially when historical mean is below 70.
- Forecasts should be adjusted downward by 1–2% for each day after a price spike exceeding 72.
- When true price exceeds forecast by >5% for 3 consecutive days, reduce next forecast by 3–5% to avoid overconfidence.
- Model underestimates downward trends — when true price falls below 65, forecast should be lowered by 2–3% per day until stabilization.
